description.value:
A brass pocketwatch whose hands occasionally stutter, reverse, or spin wildly before settling on what should be the correct local time—if "correct" means anything in a place where Markop and Remi discovered the decaying Clockwork Room on Highsun 23, where time itself is visibly rotting away. The inside cover holds a tiny phrase etched in Archie's meticulous script: 'Time is a hallway, not a line.' This was his working thesis after studying the Oracle's experiments, after seeing the oak tree pulsating with crystalline energy in the Fractured Atrium, after witnessing firsthand how the Oracle was cutting and splicing timelines like film reels.

The watch is Archie's early, crude attempt to navigate temporal inconsistencies and feel the "cuts" where reality has been edited. He wore it constantly during his time in the manor, checking it obsessively not to know what time it was but to know if time was still functioning properly. When the hands spun backward, he knew a planar breach was imminent. When they froze entirely, he knew he'd stumbled into a pocket of locked time. And when they showed times that hadn't happened yet or had already been edited out of the timeline, he knew the Oracle was nearby, working his terrible art.

While carried, you always know the local time and date in 1040 BF, even across planes and in time‑warped areas of Raventree or Shadeward Manor. Once per long rest, you can flip the cover open and ask, "Is this a hinge moment?" The DM answers yes or no based on whether your next major decision in the next 10 minutes is likely to lock out a significant timeline branch or irrevocably alter the course of events. Occasionally, instead of an answer about the present, the watch shows you a one‑sentence glimpse of a timeline where Archie succeeded in the Shattered Ritual and reality merged cleanly. It is never reassuring.
description.chat: The watch ticks wrong for a heartbeat, then clicks into a beat that hurts your head but feels truer.

unidentified.name: Odd Brass Watch
unidentified.description: A pocketwatch whose hands sometimes move the wrong way before settling. The ticking is irregular, sometimes speeding up or slowing down without any apparent cause, and occasionally stopping entirely for several seconds before resuming. The brass case is worn smooth from constant handling, and the chain has been replaced multiple times with mismatched links of varying metals and styles.

description.value:
A cracked crystalline tablet etched with the stylized "W" of Wahbook, its surface marred by dark fingerprints that refuse to wipe clean—likely vampire‑touched during Archie's time at the Shadow Estate. This is the same device Archie used to broadcast his public confession about the Greenhouse Inferno on Highsun 20, attempting to control the narrative before the Mages' Guild could spin it against him. The screen is perpetually dark but occasionally flickers with ghost‑posts from alternate timelines, showing feeds where Archie never confessed, where the greenhouse never burned, where he died on the airship instead of escaping.

The confession itself was a disaster. Instead of justifying his actions, it inflamed the Mages' Guild, gave ammunition to the Peach Loyalists' propaganda machine, and painted an even larger target on his back. But Archie kept the slate anyway, compulsively checking it during his final days to see how public sentiment shifted, reading the comments from people who called him a hero and those who called him a murderer, unable to look away from the slowly mounting consensus that he was both.

Once per long rest, you can spend 10 minutes with the slate to scan public sentiment about one named individual or faction such as Archie Miser, Liberated Toads, Iron Legion, Peach Loyalists, or the Mages' Guild. The DM gives you a one‑sentence pulse of how "the feed" currently feels about that subject in this region or plane. Each time you use it, roll a d6. On a 1, you instead see an alternate‑timeline feed where key events unfolded differently—Archie never confessed, the greenhouse stands intact, or the ritual succeeded. This has no direct mechanical effect but can provide unsettling glimpses of roads not taken and futures that will never be.
description.chat: The cracked slate buzzes and floods with floating text, half of it from worlds that never quite happened.

unidentified.name: Cracked Crystal Tablet
unidentified.description: A thin arcane crystal slab with a spiderweb crack across it and strange dark smudges on the corners. Faint symbols scroll under the surface when held, though they move too quickly to read and seem to repeat the same fragments over and over. The crack pulses with a dim light when the tablet is touched, and occasionally you glimpse text that vanishes before you can focus on it.

description.value:
A bundle of hand-rolled incense sticks made from dried mushroom stems, rare herbs, and resins that Morel collects during her travels. The smoke they produce is thick and slightly sweet, with an undertone of something earthy and ancient that clings to fabric and hair for hours after exposure. Morel burns one stick during important readings, claiming the smoke helps clarify visions and strengthens the connection between the cards and the forces they channel.

The incense takes 10 minutes to burn completely. During this time, any divination magic cast within the smoke's area (a 10-foot radius around the burning stick) functions as though cast at one spell level higher than normal, and creatures within the area have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks to interpret omens, symbols, or cryptic messages. The downside is that the smoke makes concentration difficult for other purposes—any concentration spell not related to divination requires a DC 10 Constitution save at the start of each turn to maintain while within the smoke.

Morel carries 7 sticks of incense, enough for roughly two weeks of daily readings. She makes more whenever she has access to the proper ingredients, a process that takes several hours and requires materials worth approximately 5 gold pieces per stick.
description.chat: Sweet smoke curls upward, carrying questions toward answers that wait just beyond sight.

unidentified.name: Strange-Smelling Incense
unidentified.description: Hand-rolled incense sticks made from unfamiliar materials with a thick, sweet smell and an earthy undertone. The smoke they produce is unusually dense and seems to hang in the air longer than normal smoke, forming shapes that might be random or might be something else entirely.

This pale ivory wand that has been used by Vivesna for decades. It feels perpetually cool to the touch, and gives an uneasy sensation to the wielder.

When this wand is used as a spellcasting focus, Necromancy spells attack rolls gain a +1 bonus.

Spellcasting Focus. An arcane focus is a special item designed to channel the power of arcane spells. A sorcerer, warlock, or wizard can use such an item as a spellcasting focus, using it in place of any material component which does not list a cost.

A broken half‑ring of blackened gold with a dull, cracked red gem that still pulses faintly with command‑magic. This was once the "handler" half of a paired Entropy Ring system like the one the Iron Legion forced onto Toadburt on Highsun 21, turning him into a coerced sleeper agent with a three‑day deadline to capture the Oracle. Archie managed to snap this handler piece off during his own interrogation by Agent Malissia in the physical antechamber, intending to study it and reverse‑engineer a way to free those bound by the complete rings.

He never got the chance. But even broken, the ring stub retains enough residual magic to sense its paired counterparts and—just once per day—to jam their signal. This is how Archie hoped to give Toadburt one moment of free will, one chance to disobey the Iron Legion's orders and act as himself instead of their puppet. Whether Toadburt ever received that chance, or whether the jamming came too late, is a question the stub cannot answer. It can only pulse with the distant heartbeat of command‑magic still being transmitted somewhere in the world.

While attuned, you can sense if an active Entropy Ring is within 300 feet. You learn only "near" or "farther than that," but not direction or who wears it. Once per day, as an action, you can focus on the stub and attempt to jam an Entropy Ring in range. The bearer of that ring must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or experience 1 round of static in their orders—they know something is wrong and briefly act under their own will instead of their controller's. Each time you use the jamming effect, you must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution save or take 1d6 necrotic damage as the broken magic eats at your fingertips, aging them visibly for a few heartbeats.
description.chat: The cracked gem buzzes with distant command‑magic, like half of a conversation you can barely hear.

unidentified.name: Friendship Ring
unidentified.description: A broken half‑circle ring ending in a cracked red stone. It feels heavier than it looks, and the gold has been blackened as though exposed to intense magical discharge. The gem occasionally pulses with a dim internal light, always in irregular rhythms that suggest some kind of coded signal being transmitted to or from an unknown source.

description.value:
A collection of anti-vampire equipment that Thorne brought for emergency use, now significantly depleted after three months of extended operation. The kit originally contained holy water, garlic extracts, wooden stakes, and silver dust for creating emergency barriers. What remains is minimal: one vial of holy water (saved for genuine emergencies), a small amount of silver dust (enough for one barrier), and two wooden stakes (hidden in his luggage rather than carried on his person).

The depletion represents both the passage of time and several close calls that required expending resources. Thorne has had to defend himself against unauthorized feeding attempts three times—spawn who decided a mortal guest looked like easy prey—and each incident cost supplies he couldn't replace. He's been more cautious since the third incident, avoiding isolated areas and maintaining awareness of nearby vampires at all times.

The remaining supplies represent his last-resort emergency kit. Using them means situations have become untenable; not having them would mean situations becoming fatal.
description.chat: What's left of three months' preparation: barely enough for one more emergency, maybe two if he's lucky.

unidentified.name: Nearly Empty Supply Kit
unidentified.description: A collection of containers that clearly once held more supplies than they currently contain. The remaining contents suggest preparation for threats that the owner has been encountering regularly.

description.value:
A small tin containing Morel's proprietary blend of dried mushrooms, herbs, and flower petals that she brews into a tea before particularly important readings. The taste is bitter and slightly metallic, with an aftertaste of honey that seems to appear from nowhere several seconds after swallowing. Morel claims the tea "opens the inner eye" and makes the cards' messages clearer, though she admits the effect might be partially psychological. What she doesn't mention is that the blend contains trace amounts of a mild hallucinogen derived from shadow-realm fungi, producing subtle visual distortions that make card images seem to move and shift.

A creature that drinks a cup of the tea (requiring 1 minute to prepare and consume) gains advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks for the next hour, but also suffers disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks involving sight as the hallucinogenic effects make it difficult to distinguish real visual details from imagined ones. The tin contains enough blend for 10 cups of tea.
description.chat: The bitter tea slides down your throat, and suddenly the edges of things seem softer, more willing to reveal what they hide.

unidentified.name: Unusual Tea Blend
unidentified.description: A small tin containing a mixture of dried plant material in unfamiliar combinations. The smell is complex—bitter herbs, something floral, and an undertone of earthiness that suggests mushrooms. Whatever this tea is meant to do, it's clearly not ordinary refreshment.

A jagged shard of etched stone, about the size of a palm, pried up from the ritual floor after the catastrophic Shattered Ritual on Highsun 21 detonated Raventree Manor into Physical, Shadow, Fey, and Deep Mirror shards. The runes carved into its surface now flicker between three overlapping configurations as if they cannot agree which circle they belong to—sometimes matching the Oracle's synchronization rite, sometimes resembling the Iron Legion's containment arrays, and occasionally displaying symbols that belong to neither tradition.

In faded charcoal along the back is Archie's last legible note from the ritual chamber, scrawled in the moments before reality fractured: 'If this breaks, we break.' He was right. When the ritual collapsed due to internal conflict, missing participants, and Archie's own unstable third‑eye magic, the sigil shattered and took local reality with it. This fragment is all that remains of the Oracle's desperate attempt to align the planes, and it still hums with residual synchronization energy, trying futilely to complete a task that can never be finished.

While carrying the Fragment, you can use an action to "ping" the local planar boundary, listening for the echoes of the ritual's failure. Choose one: Feywild, Shadowfell, or Mirror‑Space. You learn whether that plane is currently coterminous, weak, or sealed from your location. Once per long rest, a spellcaster can focus through the fragment while casting a teleportation, banishment, or plane‑shift effect; if they roll on a mishap table, they may reroll once and must take the second result. Each time the reroll is used, the bearer briefly sees a vision of Archie in three simultaneous versions—one burned and screaming from the Greenhouse, one pale and blood‑drained from the Shadow Estate dinner, and one with a third eye open and weeping blood—all whispering different, contradictory advice. The bearer must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or gain short‑term paranoia about Oracles, Iron Legion, or dragons.
description.chat: The shard hums with three discordant notes, like three circles trying to overlay on the same floor.

unidentified.name: Etched Stone Shard
unidentified.description: A jagged chunk of stone inscribed with overlapping runes that never seem to stay in the same pattern. When you look away and look back, the symbols have subtly shifted, though you can never quite catch them in motion. The stone itself is cold to the touch regardless of ambient temperature, and holding it makes your fingertips tingle with a sensation like touching a live wire.

A heavy vellum envelope sealed with the Mages' Guild's official sigil in deep blue wax, given to Thornbury upon accepting the observation assignment with instructions not to open it unless "circumstances require decisive action." Thornbury doesn't know what's inside and suspects it contains contingency orders for scenarios the Guild doesn't want discussed openly—perhaps authorization to eliminate dangerous subjects, perhaps extraction protocols, perhaps something worse. The envelope is enchanted to destroy its contents if opened by anyone other than Thornbury, and Thornbury has been warned that opening it without genuine necessity will result in immediate termination from the Guild.

The existence of sealed orders is standard practice for sensitive assignments, a way for Guild leadership to maintain plausible deniability while ensuring field agents have the authority to act in emergencies. Thornbury has carried sealed orders on three previous assignments and never needed to open any of them. The envelopes were returned to headquarters still sealed, and Thornbury never learned what they contained. This envelope feels heavier than the previous ones, though whether that's due to additional documents inside or simply the weight of whatever decisions it might require remains unknown.
description.chat: The sealed envelope sits in your pack like a held breath, waiting for something to go wrong enough to justify opening it.

unidentified.name: Sealed Official Envelope
unidentified.description: A heavy vellum envelope sealed with blue wax bearing an official-looking sigil. The envelope has never been opened, and the seal shows no signs of tampering. Something about the weight suggests substantial contents, though what documents might require such careful sealing is unclear.

Found throughout the multiverse, humans are as varied as they are numerous. They are relatively short-lived, but they strive to achieve as much as they can in the years they are given. They are skilled pioneers and artisans. They are builders of nations, roads, cities, and ships. They strive to secure their place in the world and in the annals of history by creating art, amassing wealth, making laws, and questing for immortality. Their ambition and resourcefulness are commended, respected, and feared.

Humans are as diverse in appearance as the people of Earth, and they have many gods. Scholars dispute the origin of humanity, but one of the earliest known human gatherings is said to have occurred in Sigil, the torus-shaped city at the center of the multiverse and the place where the Common tongue was born. From there, humans could have spread to every corner of the multiverse, bringing Sigil's cosmopolitanism with them.

Humans of Many Worlds

On any given world in the multiverse, the material culture of humans can change from one region to another. In the Forgotten Realms, for example, the clothing, architecture, cuisine, music, and literature are wildly different in the Western Heartlands than in the frozen north of Icewind Dale.

As humans migrate, they bring elements of their cultures with them, giving rise to diverse settlements that contain people with different physical characteristics, not to mention a medley of clothing styles, customs, and beliefs.

Building a Witherbloom Character

Druids and warlocks make up most of Witherbloom's student body. A few wizards (mostly those who study the @class[Wizard|PHB|School of Necromancy|Necromancy|PHB]) and clerics (including those with the Divine Domains of @class[Cleric|PHB|Life|Life|PHB] or @class[Cleric|PHB|Nature|Nature|PHB]) also find their home in Witherbloom.

A number of rangers and barbarians study at Witherbloom as well, and some rogues learn how to create and use poisons during their studies at this college.

Suggested Characteristics. Students of Witherbloom College are equally likely to be found picking herbs for a healing tincture or riding zombified swamp beasts through the bayou. The Witherbloom Personality Traits table suggests a variety of traits you might adopt for your character.

Witherbloom Personality Traits
[[/r d6]]Personality Trait
1I love brewing up a new recipe, even if some might be repulsed by my choice of ingredients. Or the final product. Or both.
2My fashion sense is like my garden: withered, black, and weird.
3I'm going to befriend every single monster in this swamp if it's the last thing I do.
4Everything in this world dies eventually. The question is, what will you do with the time you have left?
5I know we just met, but when you die, may I have your bones? For research.
6Don't interrupt me; I'm brooding.

You touch one object that is no larger than 10 feet in any dimension. Until the spell ends, the object sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like. Completely covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again or dismiss it as an action.

If you target an object held or worn by a hostile creature, that creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw to avoid the spell.

This Peach's Castle Brick is a heavy, pink masonry block stamped with the royal crest. Manufactured by Castle Architecture during the Pre-War Era, it serves as a sturdy piece of the kingdom's history.

Effects

  • Bludgeoning Projectile: As an action, you can throw the brick at a target within 20 feet. Make a ranged weapon attack; on a hit, the target takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage.
  • Royal Nostalgia: You have advantage on Wisdom (History) checks made to recall information regarding the kingdom's architecture, lineage, or royal history.
  • Heavy and Awkward: Because of its size and weight, you have disadvantage on attack rolls made with the brick if you are using a ranged attack maneuver or trying to throw it beyond 20 feet.

Usage

  • Activation: Action
  • Duration: Instantaneous
  • Ends when: The brick hits a target or misses and falls to the ground.
  • Charges: Unlimited

Vendor: wario_land · Shipped by: Rubble Runners · Level requirement: 1

biography.value:
Toad Lee — Warden of the Toads

Level 4 Barbarian; Liberated Toads, The Wardens. Toad Lee was freed from the Vigilance trafficking barrels and became one of the people who made survival into an organized duty. He is not a decorative hero: he assigns a guard, spots routes, carries an axe, and asks what happens after the door opens.

Operational record

Lee helped hold the line against the Coat, organized fractured survivors with Speaker L, pursued Waluigi during the Lounge Brawl with deliberately nonlethal leg-targeting swings, and kept functioning after Stucky's thrown eye landed on his head. He is the brain of the Feywild operation when the plan needs a roof, a route, or a fallback.

Sheet boundary

This is a level 4 playable translation of the lore. It includes confirmed themes—axe work, Rage, Warden discipline, pursuit, and survivor logistics—without inventing legendary loot or high-level magic. The XP ledger remains authoritative: 5,790 XP, 3 AP spent, 0 available.

“Travellers scowl at us, and countrymen give us scornful names.”

In this age of the world, when shadows grow deeper with every passing year, you have sworn to defend all who cannot defend themselves. Often, your choice forces you to forsake civilised areas, to better guard their inhabitants from what lurks right outside their fences. This has made you a stranger in the eyes of the common folk, a threatening figure like those you are protecting them from.

Shadow Path

@reward[Path of Despair|TLotRR]: Self-doubt is often the way that the Shadow chooses to reach the heart of those who oppose it. For they know that the Enemy is strong and terrible and that those they protect are too naive or weak to fend for themselves. Every day they ask themselves: will my strength be enough to prevail, or will I drag down the innocent in defeat?

Level 1: Shadow-Lore

Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, and hunting the servants of the Shadow. Choose a kind of favoured foe: Beasts, Evil Men, Giants, Monstrosities, Orcs, or Undead.

You can add your Wisdom modifier to the damage roll whenever you hit one of your favoured foes, and to saving throws you make against their special abilities. Additionally, you have advantage on Wisdom (@skill[Hunting|TLotRR]) and Wisdom (&Reference[skill=Perception]) checks to find your favoured foes, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them. You also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favoured foes, if they speak one at all.

You choose one additional favoured foe at 6th level, and again at 10th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of enemies you have encountered on your adventures.

Level 1: Warded Lands

You are particularly familiar with the lands you have sworn to protect and are adept at travelling and surviving in such regions. Choose one warded land from among the following: Arthedain, Cardolan, Enedwaith, Eregion, Lindon, and Rhudaur (the Loremaster may wish to expand or alter this list depending on the chosen setting). When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your warded lands, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in.

During journeys in your warded lands, you gain the following benefits:

  • You are allowed to cover more than one role without penalties (see Chapter 5).
  • You have advantage on fatigue saving throws if the journey path (see Chapter 5) is entirely within your warded lands.
  • You can move stealthily at a normal pace, and hexes suggesting difficult terrain do not slow your Company's travel (see Chapter 5).
  • While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.

Finally, a Company including a Warden that spends a Fellowship Phase in a warded land can choose the @action[Gather Rumours|TLotRR] undertaking as a free undertaking.

You choose one additional warded land at 4th level, and again at 6th, 8th, and 10th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the regions you have visited on your adventures.

Level 2: Craft or Virtue

Also at 2nd level, and again at 4th, 6th, 8th, and 10th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

At 2nd, 6th, and 10th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list (see Crafts).

Level 2: Fighting Style

At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your speciality. Choose one of the following options. You cannot take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

Archery. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

Dueling. When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

Protection. When a creature you can see hits you or a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to the target's AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss. You must be wielding a @item[shield|PHB] or a @itemProperty[F||finesse] weapon.

Two-Weapon Fighting. When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

Level 3: Warden Oath

At 3rd level, you swear your oath as a Warden. You might choose to be a @subclass[Forayer|Warden|TLotRR|TLotRR] or a @subclass[Hunter|Warden|TLotRR|TLotRR], both detailed at the end of the calling description. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th level.

Level 3: Rumour of the Earth

Beginning at 3rd level, you can use your action to focus your awareness on the region around you. You can sense whether and which of your favoured foes are present within a number of miles of you equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1; double this value if you are in your warded lands). This feature doesn't reveal the creatures' location or number. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Level 4: Virtue

At 4th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Level 4: Warded Lands improvement

Level 5: Extra Attack

When you reach 5th level you make two attacks when you take the @action[Attack] action on your turn, instead of one.

Level 9: Long Stride

Starting at 9th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing heavy armour, and moving through difficult terrain costs you no extra movement.

Forayer

You patrol the land ceaselessly seeking to ambush the servants of the Enemy, for they are found in many places, not in Mordor only.

Level 3: Bonus Proficiency

When you choose this oath at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the &Reference[skill=Stealth] skill. If you are already proficient, or if you are in one of your warded lands, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

Level 3: Ambusher

Starting at 3rd level, you excel at ambushing your enemies. You can add your Wisdom modifier to your initiative rolls, and you have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn. In addition, you gain the @classFeature[Sneak Attack|Treasure Hunter|TLotRR|1|TLotRR] feature. The extra damage is [[/r 1d6]], and it increases to [[/r 2d6]] when you reach 7th level in this calling.

Sneak Attack. You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra [[/r 1d6]] damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a @itemProperty[F||finesse] or a ranged weapon.

You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't &Reference[condition=incapacitated], and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll.

Level 7: Harrier

Starting at 7th level, you can use the @action[Hide] action as a bonus action on your turn.

Crafting Feat

You are familiar with the difficulties encountered when crossing wild lands, and with the ways of overcoming them. You can make an Intelligence (&Reference[skill=Nature]) check in place of any Wisdom (@skill[Explore|TLotRR]) or Wisdom (@skill[Hunting|TLotRR]) check.

In addition, you can spend 1 hour and a craft slot to make an Intelligence (&Reference[skill=Nature]), Wisdom (@skill[Explore|TLotRR]), or Wisdom (@skill[Hunting|TLotRR]) check (your choice). The DC is determined by the terrain type the Company is currently traversing (as if a journey event was taking place there; see Chapter 5). The check has disadvantage if it is autumn or winter. If you succeed, choose one of the following options:

  • Choose a number of creatures equal to your check result minus the terrain DC (minimum 1), which can include yourself. For 1 hour, each of those creatures has a +5 bonus to its Dexterity (&Reference[skill=Stealth]) checks. When you reach 5th level, the bonus increases to +10. If you obtain a magical success, the creatures also leave behind no tracks or other traces of their passage for the duration.
  • Choose a number of creatures equal to your check result minus the terrain DC (minimum 1), which can include yourself. For 8 hours, each of those creatures has a +5 bonus to its passive Wisdom (&Reference[skill=Perception]) score. When you reach 5th level, the bonus increases to +10. If you obtain a magical success, the creatures also gain @sense[tremorsense|MM] out to a range of 60 feet for the duration.
  • You forage a number of pounds of food and gallons of water equal to your check result minus the terrain DC (minimum 1). The food lasts for 24 hours, or 48 hours when you reach 5th level. If you obtain a magical success, each pound of food foraged in this way also restores 1 hit point to the creature eating it during a short or long rest.

Virtues of the Hobbits Feat (Prerequisite: Hobbit or Bree-Hobbit Culture)

Hobbits are a little people, but their resourcefulness far exceeds their stature. You have learnt how to exploit your small size to your advantage in a fight.

  • Increase your Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • Medium or larger creatures cannot gain advantage on attack rolls against you while you are not &Reference[condition=incapacitated].
  • You don't provoke @action[opportunity attack||opportunity attacks] from Medium or larger creatures.

Mastery: Cleave. If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

Mastery: Slow. If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.
A Quiver holds up to 20 Arrows.

Arrows are used with a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield.

Arrows are typically stored in a @item[Quiver|XPHB] (bought separately).

biography.value:
The Scourge of Probability

In a world tearing itself apart, Waluigi stands as a testament to the power of spite. A lanky silhouette of purple misery and surprising competence, he has carved a niche in the War-Torn Mushroom Kingdom not as a hero, but as a survivor who refuses to be ignored.

The 'Wally' Deception (1040 BF)

For weeks, Waluigi operated under the alias 'Wally,' a humble, mustache-less scout for the Iron Legion. He successfully infiltrated the party, feeding intel to the Legion until the hijacking of the airship Vigilance. The reveal of his identity was theatrical, devastating, and cemented his reputation as a master actor, though he lost his favorite fake mustache in the process.

The 'Friendly Fire' Incident

During the chaos aboard the Vigilance (Day 12), Waluigi unleashed a powerful Cone of Cold spell intended for Iron Legion boarders. However, due to his absolute lack of concern for collateral damage, he froze the toad ally Eager solid and hospitalized the newcomer FNG Remi. He maintains to this day that Eager 'walked into the crossfire' and that he actually saved them by cooling the room down.

The Feywild Trauma

After the Shattered Ritual at Raventree Manor (Day 21), Waluigi fell into the Feywild reflection of the estate. There, his leg was shattered by a Guardian Butterfly. He was saved by Sprites who used aggressive rapid-growth magic to knit the bone back together. The leg is now stronger but twitches with chaotic fey energy, giving him an unnatural, bouncy gait.

details.ideal: Recognition. Mario gets parades, Luigi gets sympathy, Wario gets paid. I get an encyclopedia and I wrote it myself. (Chaotic)
details.bond: Wario's ledger. I did not agree to the debt, I do not accept the debt, and I have memorised every line of it.
details.flaw: I cannot let a slight go, and I cannot tell the difference between a slight and a Tuesday.
details.appearance: Absurdly tall, absurdly thin, moustache waxed to a point sharp enough to file a grievance with. The left leg does not always arrive at the same time as the rest of him.
details.trait:
I am the greatest athlete in the Mushroom Kingdom and I will explain why, at length, unprompted.
I keep records on everyone. Everyone.

description.value: Author of the encyclopedia, reluctant employee of Wario's Enterprise, and the only person present at most of these events who took notes.
Self-taught, aggressively so. Waluigi maintains that he invented ice magic and that the existing literature is plagiarism.
Six of his eight spells deal damage and four of those are cold. Evocation is simply what he already does, written down.

Intelligence is his spellcasting ability. Spell save DC 12, spell attack +4. Slots at level 5: four 1st, three 2nd, two 3rd.

His Intelligence is 13, so these numbers are modest. That is the honest consequence of a Wizard build on this statblock.
Once per day on a short rest, recover expended spell slots totalling up to 3 levels, none above 5th.
Copying an evocation spell into the spellbook costs half the usual time and gold.

When he casts an evocation spell of 1st level or higher, he may choose 2 creatures to automatically succeed on their save and take no damage. Waluigi has never once included an ally in the blast on purpose, and says so loudly whenever he does.
Creatures that succeed on a save against his cantrips still take half damage. Available from wizard level 6 — listed here for the next level-up.

Rare Magic Weapon (+1). This is no ordinary piece of sporting equipment. Looted from the ruins of the Grand Tennis Academy during the early years of the Civil War, this racket has been modified with illegal enchantments by Wario's artificers. The frame is reinforced with blackened steel, and the strings are woven from the gut of a Phase Spider, vibrating with a low, dissonance hum that sets teeth on edge.

When swung, the racket pulls kinetic energy from the air, manifesting glowing purple projectiles of force. It functions as both a mace and a wand, allowing Waluigi to strike distant foes with the same impact as a melee blow.
description.chat: Waluigi pirouettes, the strings of his racket screaming with purple energy. He serves a ball of pure force that cracks the air like thunder. 'Game, Set, Match!'

unidentified.name: Strange Netted Club
unidentified.description: A strange, club-like weapon with a wide, netted head. It feels oddly balanced, top-heavy yet light. The strings are a dark, shimmering purple material you don't recognize, and holding it gives you a mild static shock.

description.value:
A heavy, ominous tome bound in yellow leather that smells faintly of garlic and greed. The pages are filled with frantic scribblings in Waluigi's hand and aggressive red stamps from Wario.

The final page lists a current outstanding balance of 900,000,000,000,000 (900 Trillion) Gold Coins. The ink seems to be enchanted to glow brighter when Waluigi is idle, serving as a constant, terrifying reminder of his obligations. Possession of this book imparts a sense of crushing anxiety, but also a desperate, manic drive to succeed.
description.chat: Waluigi clutches the book to his chest, his eyes darting around wildly. 'I have to pay him back... I have to pay him back or he'll take my knees!'

unidentified.name: Locked Yellow Tome
unidentified.description: A thick, leather-bound book with a heavy iron lock. It radiates an aura of overwhelming stress and anxiety. You feel poorer just holding it.

description.value:
Waluigi channels his frustration into his legs, delivering a rapid-fire series of stomps that can bury an opponent into the earth.

Effect: Make a melee spell attack. On a hit, the target takes 3d10 Bludgeoning damage. If the target is Medium or smaller and standing on loose earth or ground, they must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be driven waist-deep into the ground, becoming Restrained. A creature can use an action to dig themselves out.
description.chat: Waluigi's legs blur into a violet cyclone of violence. He stomps the target repeatedly, driving them into the dirt like a nail.

description.value:
Waluigi does not play fair. He never has, and he never will.

Reaction: When a creature Waluigi can see within 30 feet makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, Waluigi can use his reaction to interfere. This manifests as throwing pocket sand, shouting a demotivating insult, or reflecting light off his racket into their eyes. The target suffers Disadvantage on the roll.
description.chat: Just as you act, Waluigi shouts, 'YOU CHEATED!' and kicks dirt in your face.

description.value:
These aren't standard military ordnance; these are WarioWare™ originals. Each black sphere has two wind-up feet and a pair of eyes that glare with malice.

Action: Waluigi winds the key and throws the bomb up to 40 feet. It lands, walks 5 feet toward the nearest creature (friend or foe), and detonates. 20ft Radius. DC 15 Dexterity Save. 4d6 Fire + 4d6 Bludgeoning damage.
description.chat: Waluigi chucks a bomb. It lands on its feet, looks at you, and sizzles aggressively.

unidentified.name: Wind-up Iron Spheres
unidentified.description: A heavy black iron sphere with a wind-up key on the back and painted white eyes. It feels warm to the touch and vibrates slightly, as if something inside is walking.

description.value:
A leather pouch containing the remnants of Waluigi's greatest acting role. Inside is a forged Iron Legion identification card for 'Wally,' a mustache-less scout from the 4th Recon Division. Also included is a small razor (used to shave his iconic mustache for the role), spirit gum, and a collection of fake noses.

Waluigi keeps this kit in pristine condition, viewing it as proof of his superior intellect and espionage capabilities, despite the disastrous end to the mission aboard the Vigilance.
description.chat: Waluigi holds up an ID card. 'See? Wally is a legitimate businessman! Waluigi is innocent!'

unidentified.name: Disguise Kit
unidentified.description: A leather pouch containing the remnants of Waluigi's greatest acting role. Inside is a forged Iron Legion identification card for 'Wally,' a mustache-less scout from the 4th Recon Division. Also included is a small razor (used to shave his iconic mustache for the role), spirit gum, and a collection of fake noses.

description.value:
Weapon (Whip), Rare (Requires Attunement). This is not a crafted weapon, but a living cutting from the Feywild Manor's Rose Garden. Waluigi tore it from the earth during his escape from the Hag's Hut (Day 22). The stem is thick, woody, and lined with thorns that seem to lengthen when the wielder is angry.

The rose blooms perpetually with a deep, bruised purple flower. When snapped, it releases a scent of old perfume and bitter disappointment. It deals an additional 1d6 Psychic damage on a hit, as the target is overwhelmed by feelings of inadequacy.

'She loves me... she loves me not... WALUIGI DOESN'T CARE!'
description.chat: Waluigi snaps the thorny vine. It wraps around the target's limb, the thorns digging in deep as psychic whispers of failure assault their mind.

unidentified.name: Thorny Rose Vine
unidentified.description: A long, coiled vine with a single, unwithering purple rose at the tip. The thorns are razor-sharp and seem to drip a faint, translucent ichor. It twitches in your hand, reacting to your mood.

description.value:
Wondrous Item, Rare. A makeshift medical device crafted by the Sprites of the Feywild Greenhouse (Day 22). After the Guardian Butterfly shattered Waluigi's leg, the sprites used aggressive rapid-growth vines and hardened silk to knit the bone back together in seconds.

The splint has fused with Waluigi's pant leg and skin. It pulses with chaotic life energy. While wearing it, Waluigi's movement speed increases by 10 feet, but he suffers a -2 penalty to Stealth checks due to the audible creaking of the magical vines.
description.chat: The vines around Waluigi's leg pulse with green light, propelling him forward with an unnatural, bouncy gait.

unidentified.name: Glowing Vine Brace
unidentified.description: A rigid brace made of glowing green vines and hardened, opalescent silk. It looks incredibly uncomfortable and smells like fresh-cut grass and antiseptic.

description.value:
Unique Item. A crude magical communication device consisting of a jagged yellow crystal jammed into a brass horn. It is strictly a one-way communication channel.

At random intervals (usually when Waluigi is trying to sleep or sneak), the crystal glows, and Wario's voice screams out demands for the 900 Trillion Coin Debt. Waluigi cannot turn it off, only muffle it with a sock. Possession of this item imposes Disadvantage on Wisdom Saving Throws due to chronic stress.
description.chat: The device vibrates violently. A distorted voice screams: 'HAVE YOU GOT THE MONEY YET?! WAH-HA-HA!'

unidentified.name: Shrieking Crystal Horn
unidentified.description: A brass horn fused with a jagged yellow crystal. It vibrates constantly and radiates an aura of overwhelming anxiety.

description.value:
A plate-sized, iridescent scale ripped from the Guardian Butterfly that blocked the upper hallway of the Feywild Manor (Day 26). It shimmers with hypnotic patterns.

Waluigi keeps this as a trophy of the creature that broke his leg. He plans to sell it to the Deephold Smithing Guild, claiming he 'suplexed the beast single-handedly.'
description.chat: Waluigi polishes the giant scale. 'A trophy for the victor! Waluigi is number one!'

unidentified.name: Giant Iridescent Scale
unidentified.description: A massive, lightweight scale that shifts color from emerald green to deep violet. It is covered in a fine, powdery dust that irritates the nose.

description.value:
A fancy hors d'oeuvre stolen from the Orange Heir's Banquet (Day 22). To the naked eye, it looks like a delicious shrimp tart. However, anyone with True Sight or who succeeds on a DC 15 Investigation check sees it for what it is: a severed goblin finger on a moldy cracker.

Effect: If eaten, the creature must make a DC 16 Constitution save or be Poisoned for 24 hours. While poisoned, they hallucinate that everyone around them is wearing masquerade masks.
description.chat: Waluigi offers the tart. 'Try the shrimp! It has a... unique texture.'

unidentified.name: Fancy Shrimp Tart
unidentified.description: A delicately plated appetizer that looks mouth-watering, though it smells faintly of wet earth and formaldehyde.

description.value:
A fried control circuit ripped from the console of the Airship Vigilance during the hijacking (Day 4). Waluigi grabbed it hoping it was the key to the autopilot, but instead, it just turned off the coffee machine.

He keeps it in his pocket, convinced he can use it to hotwire another vehicle someday. It sparks occasionally.
description.chat: Waluigi fiddles with the sparking chip. 'Technically, this makes Waluigi the captain!'

unidentified.name: Sparking Crystal Chip
unidentified.description: A jagged piece of green crystal etched with gold circuitry. It smells of ozone and burnt coffee.

description.value:
Ammunition (+1). A canister of three heavy rubber balls infused with Force magic. These are the ammunition for Waluigi's Void Racket. When hit by the racket, they do not bounce; they accelerate, punching through wood and stone.

They are painted with an inverted 'L' symbol, which Waluigi has crudely drawn over with a purple marker to make an upside-down 'L' (Gamma).
description.chat: Waluigi loads a glowing purple ball. 'Service!'

unidentified.name: Heavy Rubber Spheres
unidentified.description: A canister containing three heavy, dense rubber spheres. They are cold to the touch and hum with a low vibration.

description.value:
Consumable. Confiscated from a drunk Satyr during the Guest Wing Eviction (Day 25). When the string is pulled, it explodes with a deafening BANG and a cloud of glitter.

Effect: Creatures within 10 feet must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution save or be Blinded until the end of their next turn. The glitter remains for 1d4 weeks and is impossible to fully clean off.
description.chat: Waluigi pulls the string. POP! 'Happy Waluigi Day!'

unidentified.name: Colorful Party Tube
unidentified.description: A colorful cardboard tube with a string hanging from the bottom. It rattles when shaken.

description.value:
A crumpled, water-damaged photograph of Mario and Luigi shaking hands with Princess Peach. Waluigi has aggressively scratched out their faces with a purple ink quill, tearing the paper in the process. He has drawn himself in the background, towering over them, holding a bag of gold.

It is a pathetic, angry little artifact that he keeps in his breast pocket, close to his heart.
description.chat: Waluigi stares at the photo, muttering. 'Cheaters... all of them. But Waluigi will show them all.'

unidentified.name: Torn Photograph
unidentified.description: A folded, stained photograph. You can see red and green colors, but the faces have been violently scratched out.

description.value:
A brass cog that fell off the mechanical hound Mossy (also known as Steely) during the escape from the Hag's Hut. Waluigi picked it up, intending to throw it at a guard, but kept it after realizing it was made of high-quality brass.

He occasionally talks to the cog when he's lonely.
description.chat: Waluigi flips the cog in his hand. 'Even the dog is made of money in this place.'

unidentified.name: Brass Gear
unidentified.description: A heavy brass gear covered in grease and faint teeth marks.

description.value:
A sack of hard-shelled nuts Waluigi gathered in the Feywild forest. He has branded each one by carving a 'W' into the shell.

Effect: They are incredibly hard. Waluigi uses them as distraction items (throwing them to make noise) or as improvised caltrops. Stepping on one deals 1 piercing damage and requires a DC 10 Dex save to avoid swearing loudly.
description.chat: Waluigi tosses a nut. CRACK.

unidentified.name: Bag of Hard Nuts
unidentified.description: A burlap sack filled with nuts. Someone has carved a jagged 'W' into every single one.

description.value:
An elegant invitation printed on human skin vellum, inviting the holder to the Orange Heir's Banquet. The ink smells of rot. Waluigi stole this from a guest he knocked unconscious in the garden.

Text: 'The Rot is Ripe. The Time is Nigh. Come feed.' Waluigi uses it to pick his teeth.
description.chat: Waluigi waves the invitation. 'I'm on the list! Waluigi is a V-I-P!'

unidentified.name: Wax-Sealed Envelope
unidentified.description: A heavy envelope sealed with orange wax. The paper feels disturbingly soft and warm, like skin.

description.value:
A tin of mustache wax Waluigi crafted using sap from the Feywild trees. It holds his mustache in a gravity-defying shape that is sharp enough to pop a balloon.

Effect: Grants Advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks, but attracts bees.
description.chat: Waluigi twirls his mustache. It stays perfectly rigid, gleaming in the light.

unidentified.name: Purple Styling Paste
unidentified.description: A small tin containing a purple, sticky paste. It smells heavily of lavender and ozone.

description.value:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon. A tattered, high-collared purple cape. It was originally a curtain in Raventree Manor that Waluigi tore down and tied around his neck for dramatic effect.

Effect: The cape billows dramatically even when there is no wind. Once per day, when Waluigi fails a saving throw, he can use his reaction to whine loudly, allowing him to reroll the save. He must use the new roll.
description.chat: Waluigi swirls his cape over his face. 'You didn't win! Waluigi wasn't ready!'

unidentified.name: Tattered Purple Curtain
unidentified.description: A heavy, velvet curtain that has been crudely cut into the shape of a cape. It is stained with wine and dust.

description.value:
A heavy iron key encrusted with dried plant matter. This key opens the bio-lock to the Vine Room in the Feywild Manor (Day 25), where Waluigi nearly died before incinerating the plants with fire magic.

He keeps it as a reminder that 'Plants are bad, fire is good.'
description.chat: Waluigi holds up the key. 'This opens the room of pain. We don't go there anymore.'

unidentified.name: Vine-Wrapped Key
unidentified.description: An old iron key wrapped in dead, dried vines. The metal is warm.

description.value:
Waluigi's left leg was shattered by a Guardian Butterfly in the Feywild Manor and rebuilt by Sprites using chaotic, rapid-growth magic. The bone density is uneven, and the leg occasionally phases in and out of the Ethereal Plane.

Effect: Waluigi ignores difficult terrain. Additionally, he can use his Bonus Action to Dash or Disengage. When he does so, purple rose petals trail in his wake.

A dusty bottle of wine stolen from the cellars of the Feywild Manor during the 'Satyr Eviction' (Day 25). The liquid inside shifts color from green to purple.

Effect: Consuming this wine acts as a Potion of Heroism (10 Temp HP, Bless effect), but for the next hour, the drinker cannot speak without rhyming. Failing to rhyme causes 1d4 psychic damage.
description.chat: Waluigi uncorks the bottle with his teeth. 'Time for a drink, to help me think!'

unidentified.name: Moss-Covered Wine
unidentified.description: A bottle of wine covered in moss. The label is written in Sylvan and moves when you look at it peripherally. It smells like elderberries and mischief.

description.value:
In the spellbook, not yet castable: this is a level 5 spell and Waluigi is level 5. It becomes available when he gains slots of that level.

You unleash a blast of cold air. Each creature in a 60-foot Cone originating from you makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 8d8 Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature killed by this spell becomes a frozen statue until it thaws.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 5.

materials.value: a small crystal or glass cone

description.value:
You create a shard of ice and fling it at one creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Piercing damage. Hit or miss, the shard then explodes. The target and each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 Cold damage.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The Cold damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 1.

materials.value: a drop of water or a piece of ice

description.value:
In the spellbook, not yet castable: this is a level 4 spell and Waluigi is level 5. It becomes available when he gains slots of that level.

Hail falls in a 20-foot-radius, 40-foot-high Cylinder centered on a point within range. Each creature in the Cylinder makes a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 2d10 Bludgeoning damage and 4d6 Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Hailstones turn ground in the Cylinder into &Reference[DifficultTerrain] until the end of your next turn.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The Bludgeoning damage increases by 1d10 for each spell slot level above 4.

materials.value: a mitten

description.value:
In the spellbook, not yet castable: this is a level 6 spell and Waluigi is level 5. It becomes available when he gains slots of that level.

You create a wall of ice on a solid surface within range. You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a globe with a radius of up to 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made up of ten 10-foot-square panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. In any form, the wall is 1 foot thick and lasts for the duration.

If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (you choose which side) and makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d6 Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

The wall is an object that can be damaged and thus breached. It has AC 12 and 30 Hit Points per 10-foot section, and it has Immunity to Cold, Poison, and Psychic damage and Vulnerability to Fire damage. Reducing a 10-foot section of wall to 0 Hit Points destroys it and leaves behind a sheet of frigid air in the space the wall occupied.

A creature moving through the sheet of frigid air for the first time on a turn makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 5d6 Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage the wall deals when it appears increases by 2d6 and the damage from passing through the sheet of frigid air increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 6.

materials.value: a piece of quartz

activation.condition: creature moves through the wall for the first time on a turn

description.value:
A bright streak flashes from you to a point you choose within range and then blossoms with a low roar into a fiery explosion. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d6 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried start burning.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 3.

materials.value: a ball of bat guano and sulfur

description.value:
You hurl a mote of fire at a creature or an object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell starts burning if it isn't being worn or carried.

Cantrip Upgrade. The damage increases by 1d10 when you reach levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10).

A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

You create three glowing darts of magical force. Each dart strikes a creature of your choice that you can see within range. A dart deals 1d4 + 1 Force damage to its target. The darts all strike simultaneously, and you can direct them to hit one creature or several.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The spell creates one more dart for each spell slot level above 1.

[[2 + @item.level]]{Level [[lookup @item.level]] darts}
An upper limit of darakhul age has never been discovered; most darakhul die violently.
Your alignment does not change when you become a darakhul, but most darakhul have a strong draw toward evil.
Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

You can see in &Reference[rule=dimlight]{dim light} within 60 feet of you as if it were &Reference[rule=brightlight]{bright light}, and in &Reference[rule=darkness] as if it were &Reference[rule=dimlight]{dim light}. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

You must consume 1 pound of raw meat each day or suffer the effects of starvation. If you go 24 hours without such a meal, you gain one level of &Reference[condition=exhaustion]. While you have any levels of exhaustion from this trait, you can't regain hit points or remove levels of exhaustion until you spend at least 1 hour consuming 10 pounds of raw meat.

You transitioned into undeath, but your transition was imperfect. Though you are a humanoid, you are susceptible to effects that target undead. You can regain hit points from spells like @spell[cure wounds], but you can also be affected by game effects that specifically target undead, such as a cleric's @classFeature[Channel Divinity: Turn Undead|Cleric||2||Turn Undead] feature. Game effects that raise a creature from the dead work on you as normal, but they return you to life as a darakhul. A @spell[true resurrection] or @spell[wish] spell can restore you to life as a fully living member of your original race.

Your heavy jaw is powerful enough to crush bones to powder. Your bite is a natural melee weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with it, your bite deals piercing damage equal to [[/damage 1d4]] + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

You have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (&Reference[skill=Perception]) checks that rely on sight when you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight.

You are infused with the dark energy of undeath, which frees you from some frailties that plague most creatures. You have resistance to necrotic damage and poison damage, you are immune to disease, and you have advantage on saving throws against being &Reference[condition=charmed] or &Reference[condition=poisoned]. When you finish a &Reference[rule=shortrest]{short rest}, you can reduce your &Reference[condition=exhaustion] level by 1, provided you have ingested at least 1 pound of raw meat in the last 24 hours (see Hunger for Flesh).

You don't need to breathe, and you don't sleep the way most creatures do. Instead, you enter a dormant state that resembles death, remaining semiconscious, for 6 hours a day. While dormant, you have disadvantage on Wisdom (&Reference[skill=Perception]) checks. After resting in this way, you gain the same benefit that a human does from 8 hours of sleep.
You were something else before you became a darakhul. This heritage determines some of your traits. Choose one Heritage Subrace below and apply the listed traits.
The training and experience of your early years was not lost when you became a darakhul. You have proficiency in two skills and one tool of your choice.

In the lightless depths beneath the ground, an empire of devouring ambition grows and plots and dreams. Their cities lie out of sight, their agents infiltrate the underworlds of a score of surface cities, and their goals know no limits. To them, if you are not a member of their empire, you are food. Their empire maintains complex social structures and forges serious alliances. They scheme and plot. They hunger for the flesh of the living. They are the ghoulish darakhul.

Into the Big, Wide World

Some darakhul venture into the wider world on the business of their empire. Maintaining their state requires envoys and ambassadors, messengers and scouts, traders and commerce, as well as knowledge of events in the surface world. These undead diplomats engage with races they might otherwise consider food out of duty to the empire and with a specific purpose.

Other members of their kind, however, have no such obligations. For adventuring darakhul, those in self-imposed exile, or those who never belonged to a darakhul empire, the quest to master their own hunger, to transcend their role as predators of sentient beings, is as much a part of their journey as the current quest. These characters typically want to grow beyond their ghoulish appetites and regain some part of their former lives in the cultures and societies of the world's surface. No one knows better than the darakhul that they can't overcome their nature unless they confront it.

But no matter how urbane or well-controlled the rare diplomat or merchant might seem to be, the prejudice of the living against the undead is powerful and visceral. Humanity views the darakhul with suspicion if not outright hostility, and it is difficult — but not impossible — for a darakhul to allay those fears.

The Cut of Your Cloak

A quality disguise is one of the best tools for a darakhul trying to make its way among the breathing. Almost all darakhul traveling on the surface maintain a disguise kit and a concealing outfit to match their cover identity. With a good costume, a darakhul might pass unchallenged among humans for a long time. Possibilities include the wrappings of a leper, enshrouding robes, veils, or the head-to-toe garb of the desert peoples. Each of these disguises requires appropriate details to help the deception withstand scrutiny: the right language skills along with knowledge of the region and its customs.

Even a convincing disguise doesn't explain a darakhul's need to eat alone and behind closed doors. Darakhul can use cultural or religious requirements to justify such behavior in most situations. In cases where a costume and a cover identity are impractical, a skillful application of cosmetics and a few gold coins slipped into the right hands are often enough to make a request for privacy seem more reasonable. Ensuring a sufficient supply of raw meat is a challenge left to the darakhul's imagination.

Darakhul Characters

Both ordinary ghouls and darakhul arise from the infected corpses of other races. Most traits of the previous race are gone when the creature rises as a darakhul, although each darakhul carries some traits of their previous form (see the Heritage Subraces). Still, most of a darakhul's cosmetic features, such as supple skin or a long beard, fade over time into the gaunt, skull-like face, fanged maw, and taut, gray skin of a ghoulish undead.

Heritage Subraces

Before the terrible scourge of darakhul fever (see Tome of Beasts) transformed you into an undead creature, you belonged to another race. Although your undead self now rules you, some remnant of your past form clings to you, making you different from the darakhul created from other races. Sometimes you retain a trait, but more likely you now have a trait that is a corruption of one you once possessed. For example, the elemental spark in a dragonborn is perverted into one of a more necrotic bent. The luck inherent in a halfling's spirit twists into a power that brings ill fortune to their enemies.

Looking Alive

To pass for a living creature, a darakhul needs a convincing costume, matching language and speech patterns, and appropriate mannerisms and behavior. The best tactic for most darakhul is to mimic the cultures they lived in while alive, because they have a lifetime (if a short one) of knowledge to draw on. Whether it's better to try to blend into the local culture is an open question. Someone who looks just like everyone else on the street draws less attention than someone who looks like an exotic foreigner—but a person who looks like everyone else yet acts oddly can rouse even more suspicion than the exotic stranger, especially in a crossroads of cultures where foreign travelers are common.

Under normal circumstances, a darakhul with a careful disguise can move among the living without rousing suspicion. As with any ability check, dice should be brought or a challenge. If, for example, a darakhul gets involved in a chase or a battle in a crowded city market, there's a chance a bystander might notice the pallor of undead flesh beneath a flapping cloak or the rictus grin inside a deep hood that's momentarily pushed back. Palace guards inspect supplicants to the Queen more carefully than an innkeeper or a merchant inspects customers. If rumors get around that there are murderers, monsters, or darakhul loose in the city, everyone is more alert.

In those situations, the GM can call for a Charisma (&Reference[skill=Deception]) check and either compare it to the NPC's passive Perception score or make an active Wisdom (&Reference[skill=Perception]) check for the NPC. Opposed checks should be reserved for those times when an NPC intently scrutinizes the character or is already suspicious. If a group of NPCs is involved, it's best to make one check with advantage for the group instead of one check per NPC.

Playing a Darakhul Character

Life as the ravenous undead comes with challenges for an adventurer. People revile the darakhul universally as scavengers at best and as loathsome, murdering abominations at worst. For such a being, participating as a member of an adventuring party is complicated. To survive on the daylit surface of the world, a darakhul must be clever and thorough.

One of the touchstones that provides stability in your new form is your old life. While you have urges and thoughts that are dark and terrible, memories and feelings from your life before undeath might resurface to help you cope. Sometimes these flashes are corrupted versions of your old self, manifesting in your mind in new ways. Other times the recollections and feelings bubble up unfiltered, reminding you of a time when you were alive. Both are painful, but pain can be instructive.

A major question you have to answer when you play a darakhul is, "How am I dealing with the change that transformed me into a darakhul?" Have you fully accepted your new situation, embracing your new powers and hungers as a boon? Do you fight against your urges daily, seeking to return to your old self? What were your goals before your transformation, and do you still pursue them? Are your new goals simply about survival, or are those aspirations a twisted reflection of the goals you had as a living creature?

Regardless of your current monstrous state, who you once were has a powerful effect on who you are now. The carefree spirit of a halfling, the fiendish urges of a tiefling, or the creative spark of a gnome: all of these do not leave you simply because of your new form. How do those traits manifest themselves in your now?

There is a great deal of narrative, dramatic, and roleplaying potential in that tension between the old self and the new. Darakhul may be undead, but they still must function in their own society—be it on the surface or in the empires beneath the surface. Most still have jobs to do and dreams to fulfill within their societies.

biography.value:
Biography of Wario in This Timeline

In this alternate, war-torn Mushroom Kingdom timeline—set amid the aftermath of Princess Peach's assassination in 955 BF and the subsequent prolonged civil war—Wario emerges as the quintessential opportunistic wildcard, a greedy chaos agent who thrives in the power vacuum left by fractured kingdoms and collapsing allegiances. Where heroes seek justice and villains pursue conquest, Wario simply follows the money, laughing his distinctive "Wah ha ha!" while the world burns around him.

Physical Appearance & Core Traits

Wario remains instantly recognizable as Mario's burly, inverted counterpart: massively built with a physique that combines obesity with surprising muscular power, sporting a huge head, prominent jutting chin, oversized pink triangular nose, and wild zigzag mustache that twitches when he's plotting something profitable. His signature outfit never varies—yellow cap emblazoned with a prominent purple "W", purple overalls over a long-sleeved yellow shirt, green pointed shoes, and white gloves marked with blue "W"s on the backs.

His personality is equally consistent: hot-tempered, boisterous, crude, and utterly shameless in his greed. He thinks nothing of betraying allies, exploiting disasters, or causing collateral damage if there's profit in it. Unlike more ideologically-driven villains, Wario has no grand vision for the Mushroom Kingdom—he just wants to be rich, and he doesn't particularly care whose gold he's counting or whose burning city he's looting to get it.

Role in the Civil War Era (955 BF - Present)

Wario operates as a mercenary-treasure hunter-smuggler-pirate hybrid who drifts between factions with zero loyalty. He's worked temporary contracts for the Iron Legion when they paid well, sold intelligence to Peach Loyalists when the price was right, smuggled goods for Fawful's remnant forces, and double-crossed all of them when a better deal emerged. No faction trusts him, but many employ him because he's effective when properly motivated (i.e., paid in advance).

His operation includes a loose network of agents, muscle-for-hire, and disposable recruits. Key among these is "Wally," a mysterious operative who executed the dramatic extraction of Bowser during the chaotic Aftermath on the Vigilance events around Highsun 7, 1040 BF. Whether Wally is truly loyal to Wario or simply the highest bidder remains unclear—probably the latter.

Wario maintains no fixed base of operations, preferring to move between safehouses, smuggler ports, and temporary camps. He's been spotted in Iron Legion territories, Regal Empire border towns, the lawless Darklands, and even popping up in supernatural hotspots when ancient treasure is rumored to be involved. His ability to appear and disappear seemingly at will has led to speculation that he has access to Warp Pipes, airship networks, or dimensional shortcuts that he's keeping to himself.

Notable Activities & Incidents

The Vigilance Barrel Incident (Highsun 11, 1040 BF): During a massive brawl aboard the airship Vigilance—which doubled as a trafficking operation reveal—Wario was discovered hiding in a barrel amid the chaos, apparently waiting for everyone to finish killing each other so he could loot the bodies and cargo. When discovered, he fought his way out, stole several crates of unknown contents, and escaped via emergency Warp Pipe he'd apparently planted beforehand "just in case."

The Remi Recruitment (Highsun 12, 1040 BF): In one of his most characteristically cruel moves, Wario approached FNG Remi and presented her with what appeared to be a gift—a beautifully wrapped box. When she opened it, the bomb inside detonated, leaving her severely injured. As she lay bleeding, Wario laughed, tossed her a healing potion (which he charged to her account), and casually offered her a position in his crew. "You survived! That means you're tough! Wah ha ha! You're hired!" Whether Remi accepted or told him where to shove his job offer is unclear, but the incident perfectly encapsulates Wario's approach to recruitment: explosively terrible and entirely transactional.

Raventree Manor Operations (Highsun 16-22, 1040 BF): Wario inserted himself into the dimensional nightmare unfolding at Raventree Manor, claiming to be working with the Iron Legion to investigate temporal instabilities (a lie—he was there for rumored ancient treasure). During the looping dinner raid involving mirror dimensions, Oracles, vampires, hags, and the Orange Heir succession crisis, Wario set up increasingly bizarre schemes:

  • In a Feywild-adjacent fairy village manifestation within the manor's fractured reality, Wario dramatically unfurled an absurdly long wish-list containing 2,361 items, ranging from mundane supplies to reality-bending artifacts. He priced a legendary Star Rod at "900 trillion gold pieces, non-negotiable."
  • He successfully extracted payment in the form of abstract "experience" from a confused entity named hjumpik, though what this transaction actually accomplished remains metaphysically unclear.
  • He departed the fairy village with piles of ridiculous artifacts, including: seventeen cursed monkey paws ("they're collectibles!"), a mirror that shows only alternate timeline versions of yourself, three bags of "definitely not stolen" Koopa Troopa shells, and what he claimed was "the original recipe for Peach's cake" (authentication disputed).

Throughout the manor's escalating disasters—convergence rituals, planar fractures, vampire politics, Shadowfell bleed, and the succession war between Orangus Cornelius and various heirs—Wario remained focused exclusively on personal profit rather than any ideological position. He sold information to multiple parties, looted during dimensional breaches, and at one point tried to auction off a "genuine piece of the Dark Moon" (later revealed to be painted glass).

Current Status & Operations (1040 BF)

Wario continues to operate as a freelance chaos profiteer, appearing wherever the war creates opportunities for wealth extraction. Recent intelligence suggests he's involved in:

  • Smuggling operations moving restricted goods between Iron Legion and Regal Empire territories, charging exorbitant fees to both sides
  • Treasure hunting in war-torn ruins, with particular interest in pre-war Mushroom Kingdom vaults and abandoned castles
  • Arms dealing, selling weapons to whoever pays—he's been linked to shipments reaching Toad resistance cells, Bowser loyalists, and independent warlords
  • Running underground gambling operations in neutral zones, rigging the games whenever possible
  • Participating in airship hijackings, both as perpetrator and opportunistic "rescue" operator who charges victims for extraction

He has no known permanent allies, though he maintains working relationships with various criminals, smugglers, and mercenaries who share his profit-first philosophy. His relationship with Waluigi (his frequent partner in canonical timelines) is strained in this darker world—reports suggest they've had several violent falling-outs over split percentages, though they still occasionally collaborate when a job is too big for one greedy bastard to handle alone.

Combat Capabilities & Tactics

Despite his comical appearance and greedy motivations, Wario is genuinely dangerous in combat. His massive strength allows him to wield oversized weapons and grapple opponents much larger than himself. He fights dirty—eye gouges, groin strikes, thrown improvised weapons, and tactical retreats when outmatched are all standard in his playbook.

His signature moves include devastating shoulder charges that can knock enemies off airships or through walls, ground pounds that create shockwaves, and an inexplicable ability to eat almost anything and convert it into usable power (he's been documented eating bombs and turning them into explosive farts, which is horrifying but tactically effective).

Wario is cowardly when the odds aren't in his favor, readily fleeing combat if victory looks expensive or unlikely. However, when cornered or when protecting a significant treasure haul, he becomes ferociously aggressive, fighting with the desperate strength of someone who refuses to give up his gold without taking several enemies with him.

Personality Summary

Wario is greed incarnate, a living embodiment of avarice without the sophistication or long-term planning that characterizes more traditional villains. He wants money NOW, he wants ALL of it, and he'll laugh while taking it from whoever has it. He's cruel but not sadistic for its own sake—he'll blow up Remi because it's funny and establishes dominance, then hire her because capable muscle is profitable. He'll hide in a barrel during a battle because why risk injury when you can wait and loot the winners?

He has absolutely no sense of shame, honor, or loyalty beyond contractual obligations (and even those are negotiable if the breach is profitable enough). He's loud, obnoxious, and makes his signature "Wah ha ha!" laugh in situations where any sensible person would show restraint. He views the entire civil war as his personal treasure vault—a chaotic environment where traditional law and order have broken down, creating infinite opportunities for a sufficiently greedy and shameless opportunist.

Yet despite all this, he's not entirely stupid. He knows when to cut losses, when to hide, and when to run. He's survived eighty-five years of civil war not through idealism or military genius, but through pure mercenary pragmatism: if it's not profitable, don't do it. If it might get you killed, charge triple. If everyone else is dying, hide in a barrel and loot them afterward.

In a world of grand causes and terrible sacrifices, Wario remains committed to the only cause that's ever mattered to him: getting paid. Wah ha ha!

description.value: You make three attacks: two with your fists or weapons, and one shoulder charge or ground pound.
description.chat: You unleash a flurry of brutal strikes, combining raw strength with opportunistic violence in a display that's as effective as it is crude.

description.value: You deliver a devastating haymaker punch powered by your massive strength and complete disregard for fighting fair. The blow carries enough force to send opponents flying backward, and you're not above adding a headbutt or elbow strike if they're still standing after the initial impact. On a critical hit, the target must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone as you literally punch them off their feet.
description.chat: You wind up with exaggerated theatrical motion, then unleash a brutal haymaker that connects with a meaty THWACK, your target's head snapping back from the impact of your massive fist.

description.value: You lower your shoulder and charge forward in a straight line up to 30 feet, building momentum with each step until you slam into your target with the force of a battering ram.
